blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Accessible and Professional HTML

Welcome to Lesson 9: Accessible and Professional HTML. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Accessible and Professional HTML”. The goal is to accessibility basics, labels, alt text, document hierarchy and professional HTML practices.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Accessibility means that people with different abilities and input methods can understand and operate the page. Start with semantic HTML, visible focus, clear labels, useful alternative text, and a logical heading order.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select HTML. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.question: A button can only be operated with a mouse. What is the best correction?
options: Use a semantic button and make sure keyboard operation and focus are available.
Put a non-interactive div around it.
blocks.explanation: Semantic controls include expected keyboard behavior; visible focus helps keyboard users track position.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Semantic controls include expected keyboard behavior; visible focus helps keyboard users track position.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Semantic controls include expected keyboard behavior; visible focus helps keyboard users track position.

blocks.text: Application tip: in a real HTML project, choose names and structures that reveal the reason the code exists. Do not copy a snippet into a project without checking its assumptions and adapting it to the surrounding code.

blocks.question: A form relies on placeholder text as its only label. What should be added?
options: A second placeholder with different color.
blocks.explanation: Placeholders disappear during entry and are not a reliable substitute for labels.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Placeholders disappear during entry and are not a reliable substitute for labels.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Placeholders disappear during entry and are not a reliable substitute for labels.

blocks.text: Keyboard users must be able to reach interactive controls in a sensible order and see which control has focus. Do not remove focus outlines unless an equally visible replacement is provided.

blocks.question: A chart’s meaning is communicated only by red and green. What should change?
options: Use more colors of the same type.
Add labels or other visual cues so color is not the only signal.
blocks.explanation: Multiple cues make information available to people with color-vision differences and other users.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Multiple cues make information available to people with color-vision differences and other users.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Multiple cues make information available to people with color-vision differences and other users.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Automated checks catch some problems, but human review is also necessary. Test with a keyboard, zoom the page, inspect color contrast, and verify that instructions do not rely on color alone.

blocks.question: A reward begins at exactly 100 points, but the code awards it only when score is greater than 100. Which test exposes the bug?
options: Test a text value such as “high”.
blocks.explanation: Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.

blocks.question: Two validation rules must both pass before submission. Which logical structure is appropriate?
options: Use OR if either rule must pass.
Skip validation once the page looks correct.
Combine both checks with the appropriate AND condition.
blocks.explanation: AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
